title: $158 Million Became $170 Million: Reconstructing Leon Black’s Payments to Jeffrey Epstein

sources.record: Dechert LLP report to Apollo Conflicts Committee
sources.supports: $158M total, 2012–2017 period, services description, Dechert conclusions and limits.
sources.limit: Commissioned corporate review; not a judicial finding.

sources.supports: Compensation questions, lack of written agreements for at least some years, committee scrutiny of tax/estate transactions.
sources.limit: Investigative assertions and questions; not adjudicated tax findings.

sources.supports: Committee statement that true payment total was $170M.
sources.limit: Public release does not provide a full row-by-row reconciliation of the extra $12M.

sources.supports: $62.5M settlement amount and general settlement description.
sources.limit: Settlement is separate from advisory-payment totals and does not itself establish criminal conduct.

open_questions: Which exact transactions account for the $12 million difference between the Dechert and Senate totals?
What contemporaneous documents set compensation for each project and year?
How did each relevant financial institution classify and report the payments?
Which underlying wires can be independently joined to the public bank-record corpus?
not_established: That the $12 million discrepancy proves concealment or criminal purpose.
That every payment lacked legitimate services.
That every Dechert service characterization resolves later Senate questions.
That the USVI settlement is equivalent to an admission of criminal liability.
